clue.text: A nap sack

parts.note: reads like a rucksack misspelt, but is a sack you take a nap in when camping

explanation.surface: A backpack spelt oddly as two words.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'knapsack' into 'nap sack' and you have a bag for sleeping in.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded zip-up bag in which a camper sleeps is literally a sack for a nap.

clue.text: Wages and gratuity in post

indicators.note: the gratuity word is placed inside the word for post

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
a gratuity is a tip

explanation.surface: Pay plus tips arriving in the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed salary, especially a cleric's, so it is a form of pay.

clue.text: Come in to register

explanation.surface: An invitation to step inside and sign the book.
explanation.definitionFit: To come in is to go through a door; to register data is to record it in a book or system.

clue.text: I'd put in now for a position in society

indicators.note: the letters of I'd are put inside the word for now

parts.note: the present is now
the contraction's letters taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone applying today for a social post.
explanation.definitionFit: A society or club is headed by its chair, the top office holder.

clue.text: Arkwright didn't take single boarders

parts.note: the builder of the ark admitted the animals two by two, never singly

explanation.surface: A mill-owner named Arkwright refusing lone lodgers.
explanation.walkthrough: Arkwright looks like the industrialist's surname; read it as ark-wright, the man who built the ark.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical patriarch built the ark and took the animals aboard in pairs.

clue.text: In which they work thirteen to the dozen

definitions.text: In which they work thirteen to the dozen

parts.words: In which they work thirteen to the dozen
parts.note: a baker's dozen is thirteen, so this is where such tradespeople work

explanation.surface: Places where people work frantically fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talk nineteen to the dozen' means very fast; a baker's dozen is thirteen.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread shops are the workplaces of the trade whose dozen is thirteen.

clue.text: Maybe a source of income for the rector from a single benefice

definitions.text: Maybe a source of income for the rector

indicators.note: the answer is drawn out of the run of letters spanning these two words

explanation.surface: A vicar's earnings from his one parish.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads like a description of church finances, but only the first part defines; 'from' signals a run of letters inside 'single benefice'.
explanation.definitionFit: Land allotted to a parish clergyman as part of his living provided farm income or rent; 'maybe' marks it as one such source.

clue.text: Spider and fly

explanation.surface: A spider and its prey.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider is something that spins webs; in fishing, a lure that revolves in the water is also so called.

clue.text: The sort of speech that gets reported

definitions.text: The sort of speech that gets reported

parts.words: The sort of speech that gets reported
parts.note: grammar term for speech relayed rather than quoted

explanation.surface: Words that make the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Reported speech is the grammarian's other name for oblique, not direct, speech.

clue.text: Not knowing-how mend a fuse?

explanation.surface: Someone clueless about fixing the electrics.
explanation.definitionFit: To be uninformed is to be unenlightened; a blown fuse leaves you mending it without light.

clue.text: Low interest rate due to unemployment perhaps

definitions.text: Low interest rate due to unemployment perhaps

parts.words: Low interest rate due to unemployment perhaps
parts.note: low interest means boredom, which having no work can bring

explanation.surface: Finance jargon about cheap borrowing in a slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low interest rate' reads as banking; here it is a low degree of interest in things.
explanation.definitionFit: Listless boredom is a lack of interest, the sort idleness breeds.

clue.text: Girl from near Wigan-a six-footer

indicators.note: the answer is taken from inside the run of letters in these two words

explanation.surface: A tall Lancashire lass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall girl; it means an insect, with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: The pincered insect has six legs, so it is literally a six-footer.

clue.text: The area isn't developed as well

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Complaint that a district has not been built up either.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As well' looks like 'too'; 'as' is a link and 'well' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bore-hole in which water rises under its own pressure is named for Artois in France.

clue.text: Make harder to fathom?

parts.note: fathom is a sea measure, so make it take more fathoms to reach the bottom

explanation.surface: Making a mystery more puzzling.
explanation.definitionFit: To dredge a channel lower increases the soundings needed to reach its bed.

clue.text: Private escort that is organised

explanation.surface: Booking a discreet companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is confined to an inner circle, so it is secret or not public.

clue.text: Bowler, for example, had to agree to differ

indicators.note: the letters are made different, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricketer who had to concede a disagreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' suggests cricket; it is the hard round hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler is a type of hat, an item worn on the head.

clue.text: One in office may have to sit and take it

definitions.text: One in office may have to sit and take it

parts.words: One in office may have to sit and take it
parts.note: an office secretary sits to take down a boss's spoken words

explanation.surface: An official forced to endure criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sit and take it' suggests suffering abuse; it means taking down spoken words.
explanation.definitionFit: Words spoken aloud for a typist to write down are what a secretary takes.

clue.text: He struggled to maintain faith in the past

definitions.text: He struggled to maintain faith in the past

parts.words: He struggled to maintain faith in the past
parts.note: describes a medieval knight fighting for Christianity in the Holy Land

explanation.surface: A man who found belief hard long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Struggled to maintain faith' suggests doubt; it means fought to uphold the faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval knights who fought for Christendom in the Holy Land were holy warriors.

clue.text: Conspirators follow the flight of a plane

definitions.text: follow the flight of a plane

explanation.surface: Plotting a hijack.
explanation.definitionFit: Schemers hatch plots; radar operators who chart an aircraft's course on a map do so too.

clue.text: Urged editor to support journalists

indicators.note: in a down answer the editor's letters sit underneath, holding up the rest

parts.note: the press is journalists collectively

explanation.surface: Pushing an editor to back the reporters.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge someone is to push or insist, so pressed is its past tense.

clue.text: People of spirit

parts.note: the nation known for its whisky, the spirit of the same name

explanation.surface: Praise for brave folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests courage; it is the drink, and the adjective also names the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes Scotland's people and its whisky alike.

clue.text: Can holy orders be so calm and peaceful?

indicators.note: putting the letters in new order

explanation.surface: Wondering whether monastic orders bring serenity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holy orders' suggests the clergy; 'orders' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Halcyon days are tranquil, named from a bird said to calm the sea.

clue.text: Employment cut without hesitation

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the cut word surrounds the hesitation

parts.note: to excise is to cut out
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A job cut abruptly.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercise of a skill is its use or application.

clue.text: The best stuff available around the East

indicators.note: the stuffing word goes around the letter for East

parts.note: to stuff is to cram
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Fine goods sold in the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: The top part of milk gives its name to the pick of anything.

clue.text: Medical man imprisoned for a harmless frolic

annotationWithheld.why: Medical man imprisoned for a harmless frolic: MB inside GAOL, but 'imprisoned' must give both GAOL and the insertion, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Medical man imprisoned for a harmless frolic

clue.text: Besom offers second-class accommodation

parts.note: B is the grade for second class
room means space or lodging

explanation.surface: A broom-like object offers cheap lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: A besom is a brush made of twigs, used for sweeping.

clue.text: Principal feature of a vault

explanation.surface: The main element in a vaulted ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective arch- means chief; a vault is built of curved supporting spans.

clue.text: Shoot out from hiding

parts.note: describes firing at a target while concealed, as a marksman under cover does

explanation.surface: Firing from cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A marksman who fires from concealment is said to do exactly this; the word is also a game bird.

clue.text: Dirty room tidied up for sleeping

definitions.note: a phrase for the room in which many sleep

indicators.note: the messy letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A messy bedroom cleaned before bedtime.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormitory is a large bedroom, a place whose purpose is slumber.

clue.text: French sea shanty the crew put together sailing the trade routes

parts.note: mer is French for sea
a sea shanty is a sung chant
a crew is men

explanation.surface: Sailors singing on a French voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships carrying cargo for commerce ply the commercial sea lanes.
